# Incidence-aware inverse-rate payment and global-cell base hyperplanes

This strengthens the existing directional payment by discarding only
ACTUAL inside boundary incidences, rather than every positive-parallel
cap. It uses the same full cap law and the measure-level cap kernel.
It does not condition the separator on a geometric cell or source label.

Dependencies are candidate e3baf104c92323ce,
candidate 06f3c3316a88c7ba,
and residual-power-concavity-of-rate-defects-and-ordinary-convex-lifts-optimal-midpoint.md.
All actual selected-minimum and jointly retained cap-selection hypotheses
of those notes are retained.

## 1. The only omitted set is an inside boundary incidence

Fix an oriented nonzero gradient direction e. For an actual limiting
cap record H={a_H dot z+u_H dot X>=b_H}, let

    m_H(w)=a_H dot z+u_H dot X-b_H,
    kappa_H=e dot u_H,
    I_e={(H,w):u_H=t e for some t>0, m_H(w)=0}.

This is a Borel set in the retained cap-record/physical-point space.
The directional cap kernel gives, for every R>0,

    v_e,H(R)=A_e,H(R)+kappa_H S_e,H(R),
    A_e,H(R)=integral_(s>R) alpha_e,H(dw,ds)/s,
    S_e,H(R)=integral_(s>R) section_e,H(dw,ds)/s.          (1)

The measures A,S are positive. S=0 unless u_H is parallel to e, and
is supported on m_H=0. The actual inverse density v_e,H is positive.
These are the canonical right-continuous versions proved in the
moving-hinge note. The identities hold jointly with the original cap
law theta; they may be tested by bounded Borel functions of (H,w).

For a nonparallel cap, A=v_e,H. For a negative-parallel cap, A>=v_e,H
because kappa_H<0. For a positive-parallel cap, A equals v_e,H OFF its
boundary plane and remains nonnegative on that plane. Consequently

    A_e,H(R)>=1_((H,w) notin I_e) v_e,H(R).              (2)

Define the positive incidence-aware capture

    v_good(R,dw)=integral 1_((H,w) notin I_e)
                                  v_e,H(R,dw)dtheta(H). (3)

Then A_e(R)>=v_good(R)>=v_e^noninside(R). No sublaw is renormalized.
The improvement counts a strictly capturing positive-parallel cap as
soon as it is away from its actual inside boundary coincidence.

Joint Borel measurability follows from the retained cap kernels and
the Borel incidence set. Restricting the finite signed tail kernels by
this fixed Borel set preserves local total-variation right continuity
in R. The corresponding left versions use s>=R. Thus (1)-(3) are valid
at every positive threshold, including rate atoms, rather than only
for almost every inverse-rate parameter.

## 2. The strengthened pointwise payment

Apply the same moving-hinge separator inequality and substitute (2).
For every nonnegative finite convex physical f and every R>0,

    integral f dv_good(R)
      +R integral f dv_e(R)
      +integral_R^beta integral f dv_e(s)ds
        <=beta integral f dv_e(R).                     (4)

The identical formula with v_good(R-),v_e(R-) holds for the closed
surface-rate tail. The Lebesgue integral term is unchanged.

This is not an additional separator conditioning: only the positive
measure lower bound for its ORIGINAL cap-load term has been improved.
All actual cap allocations on incidence planes remain retained in the
underlying signed kernel.

Strict cap margins have their literal meaning even for the retained
inverse laws. On m_H>0, actual cap selection equals one eventually on
compact subsets, so v_e,H(R)=v_e(R) there. On m_H<0 it is zero. First
prove this for the joint inverse measures by strict-margin stability,
then use the canonical right-continuous densities to obtain every R.
Consequently

    v_good(R,dw)>=p_strict(w) v_e(R,dw),
    p_strict(w)=theta{H:m_H(w)>0}.                      (5)

Thus (4) also controls all strictly capturing caps, irrespective of
continuous-normal direction. No closed-cap boundary credit is silently
inserted into (5).

## 3. At a fixed rate, omitted incidences contain whole component supports

At any fixed positive rate, the actual directional density is a finite
positive sum of geometric-cell/fixed-fiber components

    v_e(R)=sum_j sigma_j(R).

Every nonzero sigma_j is equivalent to Euclidean measure on the relative
interior of its convex support S_j and gives the relative boundary zero
mass; atoms are included as zero-dimensional supports. This is the
residual-power theorem in the dependency above.

For any affine plane P, its sigma_j mass is therefore either zero or
all of sigma_j: if P does not contain aff(S_j), its intersection with
S_j is a lower-dimensional affine slice and is null. If it does contain
S_j, every point is incident. The atomic case obeys the same dichotomy.

In particular the omitted positive measure obeys

    integral 1_(I_e) v_e,H(R) dtheta(H)
       <=sum_j theta{H:u_H positive-parallel e, S_j subset partial H}
                                                sigma_j(R). (6)

Here v_e,H<=v_e is used before the all-or-nothing component restriction.
No equality or disjoint partition of overlapping components is claimed.
The conclusion concerns the location of possible omissions, not a
license to apply separate separator inequalities to component labels.

## 4. A single global cell turns inside incidences into base hyperplanes

Suppose a component family belongs to ONE global affine majorant

    A(z,X)=a+alpha dot z+c e dot X,       c>0,

which is nonnegative on the entire limiting canonical body and vanishes
on the supporting zero face under study. This applies to an actual
finite-plane majorant of L. Every component lies on A=0.

For a positive-parallel cap u_H=t e, t>0, its margin on this zero face
is EXACTLY

    m_H(z,X)=ell_H(z),
    ell_H(z)=(a_H-t alpha/c) dot z-b_H-t a/c.             (7)

Thus the omitted incidence is a base affine hyperplane. In a sampled
fiber z, the entire component is incident if ell_H(z)=0; otherwise
there is no omitted incidence there. This statement is independent of
the tangential density or its convex lift.

Let Q be the convex hull of the bases carrying this positive-rate
component family. If aff(Q)=aff(P), where P is the full sampled base
set, and the actual critical cap volume is Q_cap=beta M with beta<1,
then ell_H cannot vanish identically on Q. If it did, it would vanish
on aff(P), and (7) would imply throughout the physical ambient hull

    m_H=(t/c)A.

The halfspace would contain the entire limiting body because A>=0.
Its boundary has zero mixed d-volume since its continuous normal is
nonzero. Joint body/cap convergence would therefore force its actual
prelimit cap masses to converge to M, contradicting beta<1. Hence in
this full-projection-span case every omitted incidence lies in a PROPER
base hyperplane. If Q spans a smaller affine subspace, the conclusion
need not hold: the cap may contain the entire rate face while excluding
other bases outside that subspace.

## 5. Own-source exclusion and the remaining global obligation

Suppose the same plane A is active at an actual positive-L source
Y_i=(p_i,y_i), with A(Y_i)=L_i>0, and H is one of that source's limiting
critical caps. Normalize its margin as

    m_H(z,X)=a_H dot(z-p_i)+t e dot(X-y_i).

The vanishing source buffer has been taken to its ordinary limit.
On A=0 in its OWN fiber z=p_i, (7) becomes

    m_H(p_i,X)=-t L_i/c<0.                              (8)

Thus this source's positive-parallel caps strictly miss its own zero
fiber and cannot create an omitted inside incidence there. This uses
active-plane contact at THAT source; it is not asserted for unrelated
source planes merely sharing the continuous gradient direction.

A compatible lower-dimensional lift can choose a center on the rate
face. Formula (4) now counts more than the old noninside term, and
(6)-(8) constrain the discarded incidences. However the lift center is
not yet proved to lie over a globally active source base. Neither its
componentwise depth nor an interior integer point in Q transfers it
to such a source. Establishing an incidence lower bound from global
critical coverage, using these proper base hyperplanes and the exact
source exclusions, remains the distinct unresolved obligation.

## 6. Original weighted-base centers exclude every inside cap simultaneously

Keep a global affine majorant A=a+alpha dot z+c e dot X>=0 on C and
an actual positive-parallel critical cap H, with ell_H from (7).
The identity holds on the WHOLE canonical body, not only its zero face:

    m_H(z,X)=(t/c)A(z,X)+ell_H(z).                      (9)

Therefore whenever ell_H(z)>=0, H contains the ENTIRE original fiber
K_z. Write V_z for its ordinary d-volume. Since the limiting cap has
the common critical volume Q_cap=beta M, we get the closed-base bound

    sum_(z in P:ell_H(z)>=0) V_z <=Q_cap.               (10)

This retains equality on the base hyperplane. In a fiber with ell_H=0,
(9) is nonnegative throughout, and any boundary subset has zero
 d-volume because u_H=t e is nonzero. Thus neither a supporting status
nor its first-order allocation can delete this fiber's volume from (10).
The prelimit-to-limit cap-volume identity follows from the established
fiber convergence and continuous-normal cap convergence; the limiting
hyperplane has zero volume in every positive-dimensional fiber. There
are finitely many fibers. This is an ordinary original-volume statement,
not a restriction of inverse law by a source label.

Define the weighted base depth of p in P by

    D_base(p)=inf{sum_(z in P intersect J) V_z:
                     J a closed base halfspace containing p}.

If ell_H is nonconstant on aff(P) and ell_H(p)>=0, the base halfspace
in (10) contains p and gives D_base(p)<=Q_cap. If ell_H is constant
and nonnegative on P, (10) would give M<=Q_cap, impossible for beta<1.
If it is constant negative, ell_H(p)<0 already. Consequently

    D_base(p)>Q_cap  implies  ell_H(p)<0.               (11)

In particular, every original weighted-base center with depth at least
M/k satisfies (11) whenever beta<1/k. A weighted Doignon center uses
k=2^n; any previously proved sharper original-base constant may be used
without changing this argument.

The implication is simultaneous for every actual positive-parallel cap
and every global affine majorant to which (9) applies. Thus at such a
base p there is neither inside incidence nor strict inside capture of
the rate zero-face components. Every captured rate component there must
be captured by a noninside cap. This substantially sharpens the purely
affine-hyperplane description from Section 4.

It does NOT assert that a lifted-rate center can be chosen at an original
weighted-base center. The two depth problems use different fiber weights
and may have different positive base supports. Nor does the canonical
one-source-plane-per-base rule identify the geometric cell law with an
arbitrary individual inverse allocation on plane ties. To use (11), the
actual canonical source/base geometry must still furnish a rate center
on an original base with D_base(p)>Q_cap, or supply an alternative
aggregate argument that retains this strict original-volume exclusion.

## 7. Uniform exclusion at ALL surviving global deepest source bases

The current nonregular selected-minimum package has more than an
individual proper-source strictness hypothesis. The independently proved
candidate ed103e599726c87f,
Section 2, establishes for every deepest base p

    D_base,j(p)-Q_j
       >=|K_(p,j)|/2-S_max delta_max,j
       >=v/4>0                                         (12)

at all sufficiently small selected scales. Here all original fiber
volumes are at least v>0 and the maximum physical buffer tends to zero.
The applicability note invokes this result BEFORE constructing the
nonregular same separator, so its use does not assume a regular cap
response or singleton contact.

This strict gap survives the limit. The base P is fixed and finite.
For fixed p, the realizable subsets P intersect J as J runs through
closed base halfspaces containing p form a finite family of subsets of
P, independent of the fiber volumes. D_base,j(p) is the minimum of
the corresponding finitely many linear sums of those volumes. Fiber
volume convergence therefore implies D_base,j(p)->D_base(p). After
passing to a subsequence that retains the finitely many source bases,
Q_j->Q and (12) give

    D_base(p)-Q>=v/4                                    (13)

for EVERY surviving global deepest source base, including every
positive proper contact in the finite nonregular cover. In rank zero,
use the formal base depth M, as in the source theorem.

Consequently (11) excludes inside incidences and strict inside capture
at all these bases for EVERY positive-parallel actual cap and EVERY
global majorant under consideration. The cap need not belong to that
source's own group. This is stronger than the own-source formula (8).

There is an explicit quantitative margin. Let

    A_sec=|P| omega_(d-1) R_body^(d-1)

bound the total area of Euclidean unit-e sections in the bounded fibers.
For a base p with g=D_base(p)-Q>0, write u_H=t e, t>0, and let

    delta=-ell_H(p)/t>0.

The base halfspace J_p={z:ell_H(z)>=ell_H(p)} contains p and has
original fiber mass at least Q+g. If ell_H is constant, use J_p=P,
which has at least that mass by the formal depth bound. For every point
in a J_p fiber that is missed by H, identity (9) implies

    0<=A(z,X)/c<delta.

This is a slab of Euclidean e-width delta; its total mixed volume is
at most A_sec delta by fiberwise Cavalieri. Hence

    Q=mu(H)>=Q+g-A_sec delta,
    ell_H(p)<=-t g/A_sec.                              (14)

With (13), the source-base margin is uniformly negative. The factor c
of the affine majorant cancels; no unproved lower bound on that plane's
coefficient is used. If cap normals are covariance-normalized, their
positive-parallel lengths t have the already proved uniform lower bound.
Thus this exclusion is stable under the current limiting construction,
not an invalid passage from a merely pointwise strict inequality.
